work.abstract_text: Extending Araújo, Feix, Costa and Brukner's global-phase argument (2014), we answer negatively the question in Liu, Wesołowski, Thompson, Gu and Pira, Optimal query complexity for fractional quantum evolution, arXiv:2610.01940v1 (1 October 2026), Section V, page 7, unnumbered Uncontrolled access paragraph, with its prescribed branch and uniform channel criterion. For 0<t<1, 0<delta<pi and every dimension d>=2, ordinary queries have an unhalved diamond-error floor sin(pi*t), independent of their number. Retaining a pure full output strengthens the bound to 2*sin(pi*min(t,1-t)/2). The same argument gives the endpoint order of the best attainable error and classifies continuously differentiable phase functions on this branch: arbitrarily accurate ordinary-access implementation is possible exactly for integer powers, up to a constant phase.

work.title: Quantitative extensions of Araújo et al.'s phase obstruction for Liu, Wesołowski, Thompson, Gu and Pira's uncontrolled fractional-evolution question
